title: Temporal splits and look-ahead prevention

objectives.text: Construct an expanding-history synthetic temporal fold with feature-availability checks,strict pre-test label maturity and explicit exclusions/window boundaries.
Keep preprocessing/model selection inside training folds and distinguish row gaps,time/label overlap,revisions and final held-out evaluation.

blocks.markdown: A chronological row order is necessary for many forecasting tasks,butnot sufficient to prevent leakage. A decision row can contain a revised future feature or a label measured over future events. Define feature availability,decision time,label observation end and label availability separately. This own splitter assumes integer-clock same-asset synthetic samples with one scalar feature,not exchange calendars or a full financial purged cross-validator.

Test decisions lie in[start,end). Training decisions must be earlier than start,with BOTHlabel_end<startand label_available<start. Strict inequality is deliberate:labels arriving exactly at the test start are not assumed processed before that decision. Each feature must already be available by its own decision time,or the whole dataset fails validation. A test label can arrive after the test period for later scoring;it is never fed into training. No fitting occurs inside the splitter.

blocks.title: A past row can still carry future information

steps.text: Test decisions are[6,8). Row a(decision1,label_end2,label_available2)can train. Row b(decision2,end4,available6)cannot:the label arrives exactly at start6and this strict contract requires earlier availability.
Row c(decision4,end7,available8)also cannot train even though its decision precedes6. Row d(decision6)belongs to test;row e(decision8)is outside the half-open test window.

Only a trains,so training center=10. Test dfeature100transforms to90. If you improperly fit a center on train+test,you get55,letting test features affect the learned transform. A fixed no-fit unit conversion is different from learning a statistic.

Full source,max128rows,strict exact ints/no bool,unique sample IDs,deterministic decision/id ordering. No equal-spacing assumption used by this own time-boundary selector. Code shows the bad combined mean only as a labeled counterexample,not a recommended preprocessing pipeline.

blocks.markdown: scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplittrains on preceding folds and exposes gap as a NUMBEROF SAMPLESexcluded before test. Its comparable-duration interpretation requires equally spaced observations. A row gap is not automatically hours/days on irregular data,nor does it inspect label maturity,feature revisions or economic event overlap. A sufficient gap for one fixed horizon can be insufficient for variable horizons. Our explicit label-end/available checks address one chosen expanding-history boundary,not every dependency/shared-event leakage mode.

Within EACHfold,fit imputation/scaling/PCA/feature selection and the model using eligible training data only,then transform/test without refitting on test. The same preprocessing TYPEdoes not mean fitting the same combined data. A pipeline helps enforce this when fitted on the right split,butcannot repair future-bearing raw features,wrong labels or an invalid universe. For training features,use the feature snapshot at each historical decision,not today's final correction.

Use earlier temporal validation folds to choose hyperparameters/features/cost assumptions,and keep a final later holdout untouched until the choice is frozen. Repeatedly inspect the final score and revise the strategy,and it becomes part of model selection even without calling fit on it. If retuning is planned over time,simulate the actual retraining schedule and available labels. Do not claim a one-time split proves a stable future regime or fixes multiple-testing bias.

The splitter removes training labels ending/available at or after test start. It does not assert independence of remaining observations. Overlapping features,shared issuers/events,serial dependence,cross-sectional panel timing and market regimes require task-specific evaluation and uncertainty. A post-test embargo is not implemented here because this expanding training set never trains on future rows relative to that test. Other resampling designs need their own interval rules;do not call a row gap a universal embargo.

Independent transfer:move b label availability from6to5and confirm it becomes eligible;move a feature availability later than its decision and require a dataset error. Permute samples and verify identical fold content;test start/end boundaries,empty training and overlapping labels. Fit a mean or scaler only on each fold's eligible training rows,record fitted parameters,and prove changing held-out feature values cannot change those parameters. Keep final-holdout reuse and outcomes uncertainty explicit.

Sources:[TimeSeriesSplitrow-gap/equal-spacing semantics](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html),[scikit-learn leakage and train-only preprocessing](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html),[ALFREDpoint-in-time revisions](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help/downloaddata). This own strict label-aware splitter is not the scikit-learn algorithm and has no scikit-learn dependency.

summary: Historical decision order does not establish information availability. Exclude immature/crossing training labels under declared interval semantics,fit transforms only on each training fold,and preserve later holdout independence. Row gaps are not universal time/label isolation and no split certifies future performance.
